intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges, this adrenaline-packed experience offers breathtaking views of the forest and occasional wildlife sightings including toucans and howler monkeys.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Spot caimans, river turtles, three-toed sloths, Jesus Christ lizards, and over 300 bird species in their natural habitat. Between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the beach.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike
experiences.description: Trek through the lush rainforest surrounding Arenal Volcano on a network of hanging bridges suspended high in the forest canopy. A naturalist guide will help you spot poison dart frogs, coatis, toucans, and howler monkeys while explaining the rich biodiversity of the ecosystem with the iconic volcano as your backdrop.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's most biodiverse national parks with a certified naturalist guide equipped with a high-powered spotting scope. Encounter all four species of Costa Rican monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and vibrant tropical birds, then cool off on the park's stunning white-sand beaches.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Day Trek with Naturalist Guide
experiences.description: Venture into what National Geographic calls 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' A full-day guided trek through Corcovado's primary rainforest offers unmatched chances to see tapirs, white-lipped peccaries, harpy eagles, and all four monkey species. This raw, remote wilderness experience is the crown jewel of Costa Rican eco-adventure.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked budget shuttle or shared transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in and settle into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Skip - in transit
meals.lunch: Skip - in transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport food court or a late-night soda (local Costa Rican diner) near the resort if open upon arrival. Budget: $5-8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book a shared shuttle instead of a taxi to save money. Shared shuttles typically cost $10-15 USD vs $30-50 for private taxis. Download offline maps and have local colones ready. Rest up for the adventures ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a slow start, take a leisurely walk along the beachfront to orient yourself with the local area. Explore the immediate surroundings of the resort and chat with locals or staff about nearby budget-friendly attractions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest local beach for free swimming and wildlife spotting. Costa Rica's Pacific or Caribbean beaches often host howler monkeys, iguanas, and exotic birds right along the shoreline. Rent a cheap snorkel set ($5-8 USD) from a local shop and explore the reef if available.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearest town or village for dinner. Find a local 'soda' (traditional Costa Rican eatery) and enjoy a classic Casado plate — rice, beans, plantains, salad, and your choice of protein.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the resort or a nearby bakery. Try gallo pinto (rice and beans) with eggs — a classic Tico breakfast. Budget: $4-6 USD
meals.lunch: Fresh fruit from a roadside stand or local market. Grab a bag of mangoes, pineapple, or papaya. Budget: $2-4 USD
meals.dinner: Local soda Casado plate with fresh juice. Budget: $6-9 USD

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally light to allow recovery from travel. Use this day to get local SIM cards, exchange currency, and plan the rest of the trip with the help of hostel staff or locals.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk along a nearby nature trail or beach. February is dry season in most of Costa Rica, making it ideal for spotting wildlife. Look for scarlet macaws, toucans, howler monkeys, and coatis. Bring binoculars if available and wear neutral-colored clothing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local mangrove or estuary by kayak or on foot. Many areas offer self-guided or low-cost guided kayak tours ($15-25 USD) through mangroves teeming with crocodiles, birds, and marine life. Ask the resort for recommendations on the nearest accessible mangrove.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and enjoy a sunset on the beach. Head to a local beach bar or open-air restaurant for happy hour deals on local Imperial or Pilsen beer ($1-2 USD each).

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto with eggs and coffee at a local soda. Budget: $4-6 USD
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic — buy bread, local cheese, and fruit from a nearby market before the kayak tour. Budget: $4-5 USD
meals.dinner: Grilled fish or shrimp at a beachside local restaurant. Look for 'Menu del Dia' (daily menu) which usually includes soup, main, and drink for $7-10 USD

day_by_day.notes: Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a reusable water bottle, and insect repellent for all outdoor activities. Staying hydrated is essential in the tropical heat.

day_by_day.morning: Book a budget zip-lining tour in the nearest available canopy area. Many coastal and inland areas of Costa Rica have affordable zip-line operators offering 6-12 line courses for $35-55 USD. Ask the resort to help arrange a group tour to split transport costs. Zip-lining through the rainforest canopy is a must-do eco-adventure experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After zip-lining, visit a nearby waterfall or swimming hole for a refreshing dip. Many local guides will point you to free or low-cost natural swimming spots not listed in tourist brochures. Enjoy the natural surroundings and look for wildlife along the trail.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area tired and exhilarated. Treat yourself to a well-deserved meal at a slightly nicer local restaurant but still budget-friendly. Try Arroz con Pollo or a fresh ceviche appetizer.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the tour — grab a banana and coffee from the resort or a nearby bakery. Budget: $2-4 USD
meals.lunch: Many zip-line operators include a basic lunch. If not, eat at a local soda near the tour site. Budget: $5-8 USD
meals.dinner: Sit-down local restaurant with ceviche and rice dish. Budget: $8-12 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-lining in advance, especially during February which is peak dry season. Wear closed-toe shoes and avoid loose jewelry. Most operators provide helmets and harnesses.

day_by_day.morning: Take a shared shuttle or local bus to the nearest national park or wildlife reserve. Costa Rica has over 30 national parks, many with entrance fees of $15-18 USD for foreigners. Spend the morning on a self-guided hike through primary or secondary rainforest looking for sloths, monkeys, and exotic birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the national park. Hire a local naturalist guide for a 2-hour guided walk ($15-20 USD split among a group) to maximize wildlife sightings. Experienced guides can spot camouflaged animals that most visitors would walk right past.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area via local bus (budget $2-5 USD). Relax on the beach for sunset and then enjoy dinner at a local soda.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure — gallo pinto and fruit. Budget: $4-6 USD
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch or buy from a vendor near the park entrance. Empanadas or rice and beans in a container. Budget: $3-6 USD
meals.dinner: Soda dinner — try Olla de Carne (beef and vegetable stew) or black bean soup. Budget: $6-8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the national park early (7-8 AM) for the best wildlife viewing as animals are most active in the morning. Bring plenty of water and wear long pants for jungle trails to protect against insects.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a local farmer's market or weekly feria if available in the nearby town. These markets are excellent for tasting exotic local fruits (star fruit, guanábana, maracuyá), buying cheap snacks, and interacting with locals. Great for budget shopping and cultural immersion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a free or low-cost self-guided coastal walk to explore tide pools, rock formations, and local beaches. Many Costa Rican beaches have incredible tide pool ecosystems with starfish, crabs, octopus, and small fish visible at low tide. Check tide charts in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost local cultural event if available, or simply enjoy the beach at golden hour. Cook a simple meal using market purchases if the resort allows, or eat at the cheapest local soda you can find.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit and pastries from the farmers market. Budget: $3-5 USD
meals.lunch: Street food from the market — rice bowls, tamales, or fresh coconut water. Budget: $3-5 USD
meals.dinner: Self-cooked meal with market ingredients or cheap soda dinner. Budget: $4-7 USD

day_by_day.notes: This is a great rest and recharge day between bigger adventures. Use the afternoon to plan and book upcoming activities like white-water rafting or a night wildlife tour.

day_by_day.morning: Book a budget white-water rafting experience on a nearby river if accessible from the resort area. Many operators offer half-day Class II-III rafting trips suitable for beginners for $45-65 USD including transport, guide, and basic equipment. This is one of Costa Rica's top eco-adventure activities.
day_by_day.afternoon: After rafting, visit a local chocolate or coffee farm tour if available in the region ($10-20 USD). Costa Rica is famous for its specialty coffee and cacao. These tours are educational, fun, and usually include tastings.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the week's adventures with a slightly indulgent dinner at a local restaurant. Try the catch of the day prepared in traditional Costa Rican style with patacones (fried plantains) and rice.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast before rafting — eggs, gallo pinto, and juice. Budget: $5-7 USD
meals.lunch: Usually included with rafting tour or eat at a riverside restaurant. Budget: $0-8 USD
meals.dinner: Fresh fish dinner at a local restaurant. Budget: $9-13 USD

day_by_day.notes: Wear swimwear under quick-dry clothes for rafting. Leave valuables at the resort. Most rafting companies provide waterproof bags for essentials. Midweek tours are often cheaper than weekend ones.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning horseback riding tour through the countryside or along the beach if available nearby ($25-40 USD for 2 hours). This is a fantastic way to see the landscape and spot wildlife from a different perspective. Many farms offer budget rides with knowledgeable local guides.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local wildlife rescue center or animal sanctuary. Many of these organizations charge a small entrance fee ($10-15 USD) and allow visitors to see rehabilitated sloths, monkeys, toucans, and other native species up close. This supports conservation efforts directly.
day_by_day.evening: Book a guided night wildlife tour ($20-35 USD) to spot nocturnal animals like tree frogs, kinkajous, snakes, and sleeping birds. Night tours offer a completely different perspective of the rainforest ecosystem.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before horseback riding — toast, fruit, and coffee. Budget: $3-5 USD
meals.lunch: Eat near the wildlife center — local soda or packed lunch. Budget: $5-7 USD
meals.dinner: Quick dinner before the night tour — rice and beans or a simple sandwich from a local bakery. Budget: $4-6 USD

day_by_day.notes: Wear closed-toe shoes for horseback riding. For the night tour, bring a red-light headlamp as it's less disruptive to wildlife. Apply insect repellent before all outdoor evening activities.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip via shared shuttle or local bus to a nearby volcanic area, hot springs, or cloud forest if within reasonable distance from the resort. Arenal Volcano and Monteverde Cloud Forest are iconic Costa Rica destinations. Even a partial visit or viewpoint stop is worthwhile.
day_by_day.afternoon: If visiting a volcanic area, soak in natural or budget hot springs ($10-20 USD at public facilities vs $50+ at resort spas). The natural hot springs fed by volcanic activity are a unique and relaxing experience. Look for free or very cheap public hot spring access points.
day_by_day.evening: Begin return journey to the resort or stay overnight at a budget hostel near the volcanic area if the distance is too great for a day trip. Hostels in Fortuna or Monteverde can be found for $12-18 USD per night in dorm beds.

meals.breakfast: Early departure breakfast — grab and go from a local bakery or market. Budget: $3-5 USD
meals.lunch: Local soda near the volcanic area or hot springs. Budget: $6-8 USD
meals.dinner: If staying overnight, explore local sodas in the new town. If returning, eat at a resort-area restaurant. Budget: $7-10 USD

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest travel day of the trip. Plan transportation carefully and book shared shuttles in advance. Carry all essentials in a daypack. Check if overnight stay is more economical than a rushed day trip.

day_by_day.morning: If you stayed overnight near a volcano or cloud forest, take an early morning guided nature walk before returning. Cloud forests are magical at dawn with mist, birds, and hanging bridges through the canopy. Look for the resplendent quetzal — one of the world's most beautiful birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort area via shared shuttle or local bus. Use the afternoon to rest, swim in the ocean, and decompress from the inland adventure. Visit a local surf shop and consider a beginner surf lesson ($25-35 USD including board rental).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed beachfront evening. Watch the sunset from the beach, then head to a local bar or restaurant for cheap drinks and light food. Try a fresh limonada (limeade) or agua de pipa (coconut water straight from the coconut).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast near the cloud forest or volcano area before departure. Budget: $4-6 USD
meals.lunch: Roadside stop or packed snacks during the return journey. Budget: $3-5 USD
meals.dinner: Beachside casual dining — grilled corn, empanadas, or a light meal from a beach vendor. Budget: $5-8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Return transport should be pre-booked. Shared shuttles between major tourist destinations run regularly. Rest well tonight — you have more adventures ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Book a guided snorkeling or boat tour to explore marine wildlife. Many coastal areas of Costa Rica offer affordable boat tours ($25-45 USD) to see dolphins, sea turtles, manta rays, and colorful fish. February is excellent for calm seas and clear visibility.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a secluded or less-touristy beach recommended by locals. Bring snorkel gear and explore on your own. Look for hermit crabs, pelicans diving for fish, and if lucky, nesting sea turtles on protected beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final big seafood dinner at a local restaurant. Splurge slightly on a whole grilled fish or shrimp platter as a treat — still budget-friendly at a local establishment compared to tourist restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto and eggs — your reliable budget Tico breakfast. Budget: $4-6 USD
meals.lunch: Eat on the boat if included, or at a beachside soda after the tour. Budget: $0-8 USD
meals.dinner: Seafood splurge at a local restaurant — whole fish, rice, and salad. Budget: $12-16 USD

day_by_day.notes: Apply waterproof reef-safe sunscreen before snorkeling. Never stand on coral reefs. Respect marine wildlife by keeping a safe distance. Book boat tours early in the morning for the calmest water conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Use the second-to-last full day for any missed activities or a return to a favorite spot. Consider a self-guided rainforest hike, a visit to a local artisan market for budget-friendly souvenirs, or a final zip-line adventure if you want to experience it again.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local community or cultural site — a small church, a traditional fishing village, or a local school cooperative. Engage with the community, learn about Costa Rican culture, and buy handmade souvenirs directly from artisans to support the local economy.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a sunset yoga class on the beach if available (often free or $5-10 USD donation-based), or simply meditate and reflect on the trip while watching the Pacific or Caribbean sunset. Have a final group dinner with fellow travelers met along the way.

meals.breakfast: Try a new breakfast spot — look for a local bakery offering homemade pan dulce and café chorreado (traditional drip coffee). Budget: $3-5 USD
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach with market purchases — fresh fruit, cheese, crackers, and cold drinks. Budget: $5-7 USD
meals.dinner: Group dinner at a local soda or open-air restaurant. Share dishes to try more variety. Budget: $8-12 USD

day_by_day.notes: Start packing tonight and organize receipts and souvenirs. Check your flight details and arrange transport to the airport. Keep enough colones for tips, final meals, and any last-minute purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Costa Rica! Wake up early for one last sunrise walk on the beach. Take photos, collect a few shells (where permitted), and soak in the natural beauty. Do a final check of the resort room for any forgotten items.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and arrange transport to Juan Santamaría International Airport. Allow ample time — at least 3-4 hours before your flight for the drive plus check-in and security. Use any remaining colones on snacks, coffee, or small souvenirs at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with incredible memories of zip-lining through rainforest canopies, spotting sloths and macaws, surfing Pacific waves, and experiencing the pure life — Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final Tico breakfast — gallo pinto, eggs, fresh fruit, and café chorreado. Savor every bite! Budget: $5-7 USD
meals.lunch: Light meal or snacks at the airport or on the road. Use remaining local currency. Budget: $5-10 USD
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport food depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Costa Rica charges a departure tax which is usually included in modern airline tickets — confirm this with your airline. Exchange any remaining colones back to your home currency at the airport, though rates are better in town. Say 'Pura Vida' to every Tico you meet on your way out — it's the Costa Rican way of life meaning pure, simple, and good!

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Late night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort (Beachfront). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit or just arriving.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged airport transfer. Drive approximately 3–4 hours to the resort depending on location. Grab a light snack from the airport or a 24-hour soda (local diner) en route.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In-flight meal
meals.lunch: N/A – In-flight meal
meals.dinner: Light airport snack or roadside 24-hour soda/convenience stop en route to the resort

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer in advance. Keep a small carry-on bag with essentials for the overnight drive. Confirm resort late check-in arrangements. Rest is the priority tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow orientation walk along the beachfront to get your bearings and soak in the coastal surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local beach area near the resort. Swim, relax on the sand, or rent a kayak or paddleboard from the resort's beach equipment rental. Visit a nearby tide pool or mangrove edge if accessible on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along the beach. Enjoy a welcome dinner at the resort's restaurant or a nearby beachside eatery to celebrate the start of your adventure.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast – enjoy gallo pinto (rice and beans), fresh tropical fruit, and Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Casual beachside soda – try a casado (rice, beans, salad, and protein) for an authentic mid-range meal (~$10–15 USD)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or nearby beachfront restaurant – grilled fresh fish, plantains, and a local Imperial beer (~$20–30 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a rest and acclimatization day. Do not over-schedule. Use this time to hydrate, apply sunscreen, and adjust to the tropical climate. Pick up local SIM card or confirm data plan works.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided wildlife walk near the resort or a nearby nature reserve. Look for howler monkeys, sloths, scarlet macaws, and iguanas with a local naturalist guide (book through resort concierge, ~$30–50 USD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby waterfall or swimming hole in the afternoon. Many coastal regions in Costa Rica have accessible short hikes to refreshing natural pools. Alternatively, explore a local fishing village or artisan market.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a cocktail at the beach bar and watch the stars from the shoreline.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at resort before the wildlife walk – fruit, yogurt, and coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch packed by the resort or stop at a local soda near the waterfall trail (~$8–12 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range local restaurant in the nearest town – try arroz con mariscos (seafood rice) or fresh ceviche (~$15–25 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear long sleeves and pants for the early morning wildlife walk to protect against insects. Bring binoculars if available. February is dry season on the Pacific coast – expect warm, sunny conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for Manuel Antonio National Park (travel time varies by resort location – typically 1–3 hours along the Pacific coast). Begin the Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Tour with a certified naturalist guide equipped with a high-powered spotting scope. Look for white-faced capuchin monkeys, sloths, poison dart frogs, and toucans.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the guided tour, spend free time on Manuel Antonio's famous white-sand beach inside the park. Swim in the calm cove waters or hike the Cathedral Point trail for panoramic ocean views.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the resort or overnight in Quepos (the gateway town to Manuel Antonio) if distance warrants. Enjoy dinner in Quepos town.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at resort before departure – gallo pinto and eggs
meals.lunch: Lunch at a restaurant just outside Manuel Antonio park entrance – try El Wagon or a similar mid-range spot (~$12–18 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Quepos or back at resort – fresh tuna or mahi-mahi with rice and salad (~$18–28 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park has a daily visitor cap – book guided tour and park entry tickets well in advance online. Wear reef-safe sunscreen inside the park. Bring a dry bag for beach time after the hike. Park opens at 7:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Depart resort and drive or take a shared shuttle toward the Osa Peninsula / Drake Bay area to prepare for the Corcovado National Park experience the following day. Enjoy the scenic coastal drive through small fishing towns.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Drake Bay or Sierpe area. Check into a mid-range eco-lodge (pre-booked, ~$80–120 USD/night). Take a short afternoon boat tour of the Sierpe River mangroves to spot crocodiles, herons, and river wildlife.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the eco-lodge. Attend a brief orientation/briefing with your guide for tomorrow's Corcovado trek. Enjoy the sounds of the jungle at night.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure
meals.lunch: Roadside soda stop en route – casado or empanadas (~$8–12 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at eco-lodge or local restaurant in Drake Bay – fresh catch of the day with tropical sides (~$15–22 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Osa Peninsula is remote – ATMs are scarce. Carry sufficient cash. Confirm Corcovado trek booking and guide arrangements. Pack light for the trek: water, snacks, sturdy hiking boots, rain jacket, insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Corcovado National Park Day Trek with Naturalist Guide. Depart by boat from Drake Bay at sunrise to reach the San Pedrillo or La Leona ranger station. Begin trekking through what National Geographic calls 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' Spot tapirs, peccaries, scarlet macaws, poison dart frogs, and possibly a jaguar track.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue deep into Corcovado's primary rainforest. Swim in a jungle river or waterfall during a rest break. Your naturalist guide will identify flora and fauna throughout. Packed lunch consumed in the forest.
day_by_day.evening: Return boat ride to Drake Bay. Shower, rest, and enjoy a well-earned dinner. Share stories from the day over local beer.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-trek breakfast at eco-lodge – eggs, fruit, and coffee before 6:00 AM departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by tour operator or eco-lodge – sandwiches, fruit, and snacks eaten in the park
meals.dinner: Dinner at eco-lodge – hearty meal of rice, beans, chicken or fish, and fresh juice (~$15–20 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is the most physically demanding day of the trip. Wear broken-in waterproof hiking boots. Bring at least 2–3 liters of water. Apply heavy insect repellent. Listen carefully to your guide – Corcovado has venomous snakes. This experience is worth every step.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the Drake Bay eco-lodge. Optional: gentle snorkeling at Drake Bay's coral reef or a hammock morning with a book. The bay is calm and excellent for spotting dolphins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel day: Depart Drake Bay by small charter flight or long road journey back toward the Central Valley or onward to Arenal Volcano area. A domestic flight from Palmar Sur to San José (~$80–120 USD) is recommended for time efficiency.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in the La Fortuna / Arenal Volcano area. Check into a mid-range hotel with volcano views (pre-booked, ~$70–110 USD/night). Unwind at the hotel's hot springs pool if available.

meals.breakfast: Eco-lodge breakfast before departure – gallo pinto, eggs, and tropical fruit
meals.lunch: Airport snack in Palmar Sur or San José, or roadside soda if driving (~$8–12 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner in La Fortuna town – try Don Rufino or a similar mid-range restaurant with volcano views (~$18–28 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book domestic flights well in advance – Sansa or Sky Airline operate these routes. Alternatively, shared shuttles from Osa to Arenal take 6–8 hours with connections. Confirm hotel in La Fortuna has hot springs access.

day_by_day.morning: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike. Depart early for the Mistico Arenal Hanging Bridges Park or similar hanging bridges circuit. Trek through lush rainforest on suspended bridges with stunning views of Arenal Volcano. Spot toucans, morpho butterflies, and tree frogs.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, visit La Fortuna Waterfall (Catarata La Fortuna). Descend 500+ steps to the base of this magnificent 70-meter waterfall and swim in the cool turquoise pool below.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in one of La Fortuna's famous natural hot springs (Tabacón, Baldi, or Ecotermales – mid-range options ~$30–45 USD entry). Enjoy the therapeutic volcanic mineral waters under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before the hike – eggs, gallo pinto, fresh juice
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at the hanging bridges park or a soda near La Fortuna Waterfall (~$10–14 USD)
meals.dinner: Restaurant in La Fortuna – try Lava Lounge or Soda Viquez for mid-range options; casado or pasta (~$15–22 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Start the hanging bridges hike early to avoid midday heat and crowds. The La Fortuna Waterfall steps are steep – take your time going down and up. Book hot springs in advance, especially for Ecotermales which has limited capacity.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Depart La Fortuna toward Monteverde Cloud Forest (approximately 3–4 hours via the scenic Lake Arenal route by jeep-boat-jeep transfer, ~$25–35 USD – a classic Costa Rica adventure). Enjoy stunning lake and volcano views during the crossing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Monteverde / Santa Elena. Check into a mid-range cloud forest lodge (~$70–100 USD/night). Take a gentle afternoon walk through the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve – a quieter, less-crowded alternative to the main Monteverde reserve.
day_by_day.evening: Join a guided night walk in the cloud forest (offered by most lodges, ~$25–35 USD). Spot red-eyed tree frogs, glass frogs, sleeping birds, and other nocturnal wildlife with a flashlight and expert guide.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in La Fortuna before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in a Santa Elena town soda upon arrival – soup, casado, or bocas (~$10–14 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Monteverde restaurant – try Morpho's Restaurant or Café Caburé for mid-range dining (~$16–25 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: The jeep-boat-jeep transfer is scenic and efficient – book through your hotel. Monteverde is cooler and misty (bring a light jacket and rain layer). The night walk is a highlight – do not skip it.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour – the iconic experience of the trip. Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most celebrated zip-line circuits (Original Canopy Tour, Extremo, or Sky Adventures Monteverde – ~$45–75 USD). Multiple cables, Tarzan swings, and rappels through the cloud forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve (the original reserve). Walk the well-maintained trails hoping to spot the resplendent quetzal – February is an excellent month for quetzal sightings. Hire a local guide at the entrance for the best wildlife spotting (~$20–30 USD).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Santa Elena's charming village. Browse artisan shops, visit the Bat Jungle exhibit (~$15 USD – fascinating!), or enjoy a cup of locally grown coffee at a café.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast – eggs, gallo pinto, cloud forest coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or quick bite between activities in Santa Elena (~$8–12 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Trio Restaurant or El Jardín in Santa Elena – wood-fired pizza or Costa Rican fusion (~$18–26 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the zip-line tour the day before to secure your preferred time slot. Wear closed-toe shoes and leave jewelry at the lodge. The Monteverde Biological Reserve has a daily visitor limit – arrive early or book entry in advance. February offers good quetzal viewing odds.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Depart Monteverde for Tortuguero National Park on the Caribbean coast. This is a longer travel day (approximately 5–7 hours via San José or direct shuttle + boat). Take a shared shuttle to San José, then a bus/van and boat transfer to Tortuguero village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Tortuguero village by boat (the only way in – no roads). Check into a mid-range jungle lodge (~$80–120 USD/night including meals). Settle in and take a short walk through the small village.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a welcome dinner at your lodge. Listen to the sounds of the Caribbean jungle – howler monkeys, frogs, and tropical birds. Brief orientation with your guide for tomorrow's wildlife boat safari.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast in Monteverde before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in San José during the transit stop – restaurant near the bus terminal (~$10–15 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner included at Tortuguero lodge – typically Caribbean-style rice and beans cooked in coconut milk, with chicken or fish

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest travel day of the trip. Depart Monteverde by 6:00–7:00 AM. Book shuttle + boat transfer in advance through your lodge or a reputable operator. Tortuguero lodges typically include meals in their rates – confirm when booking.

day_by_day.morning: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari – glide through the jungle canals at sunrise with your naturalist guide. Spot caimans, river turtles, Jesus Christ lizards, great green macaws, monkeys, and manatees (if lucky). The early morning light is magical for wildlife and photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a guided kayak tour through the narrower secondary canals for a more intimate wildlife experience (~$20–30 USD). Alternatively, hike the short Cerro de Tortuguero hill trail for panoramic views over the park and Caribbean coast.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Tortuguero village to browse local artisan shops and learn about the community's sea turtle conservation efforts. Enjoy a sunset from the beach (note: swimming is not recommended due to currents and sharks). Farewell dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at lodge before the boat safari – fruit, eggs, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at lodge (typically included) – Caribbean rice and beans, salad, and fresh juice
meals.dinner: Final dinner at lodge or a village restaurant – rondon stew (Caribbean seafood coconut soup) is a must-try specialty (~$15–20 USD if eating out)

day_by_day.notes: February is not sea turtle nesting season (nesting peaks July–October for green turtles), but the wildlife boat safari is excellent year-round. Bring a waterproof camera case or dry bag for the boat. Mosquito repellent is essential in Tortuguero.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tortuguero. Wake up early for one last sunrise canal walk or simply enjoy coffee on your lodge's river deck watching the wildlife. Pack and check out of the lodge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Boat transfer out of Tortuguero to the bus/shuttle connection point. Travel back to San José (approximately 3–4 hours total). Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a final lunch in San José and visit the Mercado Central or Barrio Amón for last-minute souvenirs and coffee to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport for your departure flight. Reflect on an incredible 13-day journey through Costa Rica's most extraordinary ecosystems – cloud forests, volcanoes, rainforests, Caribbean canals, and Pacific beaches.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast in Tortuguero – gallo pinto, eggs, and Costa Rican coffee one last time
meals.lunch: Lunch in San José – Nuestra Tierra restaurant near the airport area for authentic farewell casado (~$12–18 USD)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security at San José airport. Purchase Costa Rican coffee, chocolate, and artisan crafts at the Mercado Central for souvenirs. Pura vida!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges, this adrenaline-packed experience offers breathtaking views of the forest and occasional wildlife sightings including toucans and howler monkeys.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Spot caimans, river turtles, three-toed sloths, Jesus Christ lizards, and over 300 bird species in their natural habitat. Between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the beach.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike
experiences.description: Trek through the lush rainforest surrounding Arenal Volcano on a network of hanging bridges suspended high in the forest canopy. A naturalist guide will help you spot poison dart frogs, coatis, toucans, and howler monkeys while explaining the rich biodiversity of the ecosystem with the iconic volcano as your backdrop.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's most biodiverse national parks with a certified naturalist guide equipped with a high-powered spotting scope. Encounter all four species of Costa Rican monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and vibrant tropical birds, then cool off on the park's stunning white-sand beaches.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Day Trek with Naturalist Guide
experiences.description: Venture into what National Geographic calls 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' A full-day guided trek through Corcovado's primary rainforest offers unmatched chances to see tapirs, white-lipped peccaries, harpy eagles, and all four monkey species. This raw, remote wilderness experience is the crown jewel of Costa Rican eco-adventure.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on United Airlines. A private luxury transfer (pre-arranged Mercedes Sprinter or SUV) will whisk you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, enjoy a welcome amenity and late-night light bites prepared by the resort.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In-flight
meals.lunch: N/A – In-flight
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome platter and welcome cocktail arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private airport transfer 48 hours in advance. Request early check-in preparation with the resort. Keep luggage light for carry-on to speed up customs. Costa Rica time is CST (UTC-6). No activities scheduled before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort morning. After a gourmet breakfast, take a guided orientation walk of the Aegean Bliss Resort grounds and beachfront, getting acquainted with the property's flora, resident wildlife (sloths, toucans, howler monkeys), and amenities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax and decompress at the resort's infinity pool or private beachfront. Arrange a 90-minute couples or solo massage at the resort spa to recover from travel fatigue. Optional: snorkeling or paddleboarding from the resort beach.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's ocean-view bar followed by a fine dining dinner at the resort's signature restaurant. Request a table on the terrace for ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort – fresh tropical fruits, eggs to order, gallo pinto, artisan pastries, fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Beachside light lunch at the resort's beach club – ceviche, grilled fish tacos, tropical salads, fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant – multi-course tasting menu featuring locally sourced Costa Rican ingredients; pair with a curated selection of South American wines

day_by_day.notes: Use this day purely for rest and acclimatization. Book spa treatments in advance as slots fill quickly. Hydrate well – Costa Rica's humidity can be intense for new arrivals.

day_by_day.morning: Depart resort early by private charter flight or luxury 4x4 transfer to Manuel Antonio National Park (approximately 2–3 hours if driving from the central Pacific coast, or a short scenic flight). Begin the Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Tour with a certified naturalist guide equipped with high-powered spotting scopes. Spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, three-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, Jesus Christ lizards, and rare poison dart frogs in one of the world's most biodiverse parks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-tour, enjoy a private picnic lunch on one of Manuel Antonio's pristine white-sand beaches (Playa Manuel Antonio). Swim in the warm Pacific waters or snorkel the rocky reef. Optional: kayak tour of the park's coastal waters with a private guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by private transfer. Freshen up and enjoy dinner at a top-rated restaurant near the resort or back at the property. Enjoy a nightcap at the resort bar under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the resort before departure – açaí bowls, fresh fruit, eggs, Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Upscale private picnic arranged by the tour operator – gourmet sandwiches, tropical fruit, artisan cheeses, sparkling water, and fresh-squeezed lemonade on the beach
meals.dinner: La Cantina or equivalent fine dining restaurant near Manuel Antonio/resort area – fresh Pacific seafood, Costa Rican fusion cuisine; alternatively, resort dinner on return

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio is a UNESCO-recognized biodiversity hotspot. Wear neutral-colored lightweight clothing and closed-toe shoes. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only. Carry binoculars. Book the naturalist guide well in advance – private tours are limited. Entry to the park requires advance ticket booking.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer or charter flight to the Osa Peninsula – gateway to Corcovado National Park. Begin the Corcovado National Park Day Trek with Naturalist Guide – venture into what National Geographic calls 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' Trek through primary rainforest teeming with Baird's tapirs, giant anteaters, pumas, scarlet macaws, harpy eagles, and all four species of Costa Rican monkeys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Corcovado trek through diverse ecosystems – river crossings, coastal trails, and old-growth rainforest. Enjoy a packed gourmet lunch in the heart of the jungle. Spot marine wildlife along the park's wild Pacific coastline including dolphins and sea turtles.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Osa Peninsula base lodge or private eco-luxury lodge (e.g., Lapa Rios Lodge or Bosque del Cabo – upgrade option) for an overnight stay to maximize time in this remote paradise. Enjoy a candle-lit dinner with jungle views.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast at resort before early departure – protein-rich with eggs, whole grains, tropical fruits, and strong Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet jungle picnic arranged by tour operator – fresh sandwiches, energy bars, tropical fruit, electrolyte drinks, and purified water
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lapa Rios Lodge or Bosque del Cabo eco-luxury lodge – farm-to-table Costa Rican cuisine with organic ingredients sourced from the Osa Peninsula; fine wine pairing available

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado is physically demanding – wear sturdy waterproof hiking boots, long lightweight pants, and insect repellent. The trek involves river crossings so waterproof bags are essential. Only 200 visitors are permitted per day so advance booking is mandatory. This is a once-in-a-lifetime experience – allow full energy for this day.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk on the grounds of the Osa Peninsula eco-lodge before breakfast. Spot scarlet macaws, toucans, and howler monkeys from the lodge canopy platform. Enjoy a sunrise yoga session overlooking the Pacific jungle canopy (if offered by the lodge).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat tour along the Osa Peninsula coastline – spot humpback whales (February is peak whale season in Costa Rica), spinner dolphins, sea turtles, and manta rays. Stop at a remote beach for swimming and snorkeling. Return to lodge for a relaxing afternoon with optional massage at the lodge spa.
day_by_day.evening: Private charter flight or scenic 4x4 transfer back to Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrive in time for a late resort dinner or room service in your suite.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Osa eco-lodge – fresh tropical fruits, local cheeses, eggs, organic coffee, homemade breads
meals.lunch: Beachside seafood lunch at a remote Osa beach during the boat tour – fresh ceviche, grilled lobster, cold beverages arranged by the boat captain
meals.dinner: Late dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort upon return – light Costa Rican fare or room service; sopa negra (black bean soup), grilled fish, patacones

day_by_day.notes: February is prime humpback whale watching season in the Osa Peninsula – request a dedicated whale-watching boat with a marine biologist guide. Confirm return transfer/flight logistics the night before. Pack light for the Osa days – only essentials.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and resort morning after the Osa adventure. Enjoy a slow breakfast and a private yoga or meditation session on the resort beach at sunrise. Take a guided resort nature walk to spot local wildlife in the resort gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart by private luxury transfer toward Tortuguero National Park on Costa Rica's Caribbean coast (best accessed via private charter flight from San José – approximately 1.5–2 hours total). Check in to a premium eco-lodge within or adjacent to Tortuguero (e.g., Tortuga Lodge or Pachira Lodge).
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your Tortuguero eco-lodge. Enjoy a guided sunset walk along the black-sand Caribbean beach, watching for nesting sea turtles (green sea turtles nest February–October). Dinner at the lodge with Caribbean-inspired cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – smoothie bowls, eggs Benedict, fresh tropical juices
meals.lunch: In-transit lunch at a premium San José restaurant if routing through the capital – Restaurante Grano de Oro or similar upscale option
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tortuga Lodge or Pachira Lodge – Caribbean-style rice and beans (rice cooked in coconut milk), fresh Caribbean seafood, tropical desserts

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is only accessible by boat or small aircraft – no roads connect it to the rest of Costa Rica. This remoteness is part of its magic. Pack light bags for the lodge as storage is limited. Bring cash as ATMs are not available in Tortuguero village.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for the Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari – glide through the jungle canals at first light when wildlife is most active. Spot caimans, river otters, Jesus Christ lizards, three-toed sloths, green iguanas, roseate spoonbills, and troops of howler and spider monkeys with a certified naturalist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to lodge for a late breakfast/brunch. Rest during the midday heat. Optional: kayak through secondary canals for a more intimate wildlife encounter, paddling silently through the waterways for up-close sightings unavailable from motorized boats.
day_by_day.evening: Evening guided sea turtle nesting observation tour on the beach (February is active nesting season for green sea turtles). Watch massive green sea turtles emerge from the ocean to lay eggs under the guidance of a certified turtle conservation guide. Return to lodge for a celebratory dinner.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-dawn snack before boat safari – granola bars, fruit, coffee provided by the lodge; full gourmet breakfast served upon return
meals.lunch: Lodge lunch – Caribbean chicken in coconut sauce, fresh salads, tropical fruit, cold beverages
meals.dinner: Special dinner at the lodge celebrating the turtle experience – grilled Caribbean lobster, heart of palm salad, tres leches cake, premium rum cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Sea turtle observation tours are strictly regulated – no flash photography, stay with your guide, maintain silence, and wear dark clothing. Tours are led only by certified SINAC-approved guides. The experience is deeply moving and conservation-focused. Tip your naturalist guide generously.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning canal boat tour in Tortuguero focusing on bird photography – Tortuguero has over 300 bird species including kingfishers, toucans, herons, and the elusive sunbittern. Visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy visitor center to learn about ongoing conservation efforts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Tortuguero by private charter flight to La Fortuna/Arenal area. Check in to a premium Arenal volcano-view lodge (e.g., Nayara Springs or The Springs Resort & Spa). Relax in natural volcanic hot spring pools with volcano views.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in private volcanic hot springs at the resort as the sun sets behind Arenal Volcano. Enjoy a premium dinner at the lodge's fine dining restaurant with unobstructed volcano views.

meals.breakfast: Final Caribbean breakfast at Tortuguero lodge – gallo pinto, fresh fruit, eggs, Caribbean coffee
meals.lunch: In-transit snack or light lunch at La Fortuna town – visit Soda La Hormiga or similar local spot for a quick authentic Costa Rican casado
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nayara Springs or The Springs Resort – upscale Costa Rican fusion tasting menu; volcano-view terrace dining; extensive cocktail and wine list

day_by_day.notes: La Fortuna is approximately 4 hours by road from San José or 30–45 minutes by charter flight from Tortuguero. Arrange private charter for efficiency. Arenal Volcano is most visible in the morning before afternoon clouds roll in – request a volcano-view room.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike – trek through the lush primary rainforest surrounding Arenal Volcano on a network of suspension hanging bridges offering bird's-eye views of the rainforest canopy. Spot poison dart frogs, morpho butterflies, toucans, and three-toed sloths with a private naturalist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Arenal Volcano National Park for a guided lava field hike along the 1968 lava flow trail with panoramic volcano views. Alternatively, enjoy a private guided kayak tour on Lake Arenal, one of Costa Rica's largest lakes, with stunning volcano backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the luxury lodge for a private candlelit dinner in your villa or at the resort's premier restaurant. Conclude the evening with a long soak in your private volcanic hot spring plunge pool under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the lodge before the hike – eggs to order, fresh fruit, artisan breads, Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the hanging bridges trail – gourmet box lunch provided by the lodge with sandwiches, fruit, energy snacks, and fresh juices
meals.dinner: Private in-villa dining experience at Nayara Springs – personalized menu curated by the resort chef, premium wine pairing, volcanic hot spring soaking under the stars

day_by_day.notes: The hanging bridges are accessible to most fitness levels but wear sturdy closed-toe shoes. The bridges are at elevation so mornings can be cool – bring a light layer. Wildlife sightings are most frequent in the early morning hours. Request a private guide for the most personalized experience.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private 4x4 luxury transfer to Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve (approximately 3–4 hours from La Fortuna via the scenic lake crossing by boat + jeep, or 3 hours by road). Check in to a premium cloud forest lodge (e.g., El Silencio Lodge or Monteverde Lodge & Gardens). Take a guided introductory walk through the cloud forest to acclimatize to the misty highland environment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve on a private guided walk – spot resplendent quetzals (February is prime quetzal season as they begin their mating displays), emerald toucanets, bellbirds, and orchids. Visit the Orchid Garden and Butterfly Garden for up-close encounters with cloud forest flora and fauna.
day_by_day.evening: Guided night walk through the cloud forest to spot nocturnal wildlife including kinkajous, glass frogs, sleeping birds, and tarantulas. Return to lodge for a warming dinner by the fireplace.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Arenal lodge before departure – hearty mountain breakfast with eggs, gallo pinto, fresh fruits, local cheese, coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Monteverde town – Café Caburé or similar upscale café known for its European-Costa Rican fusion and artisan chocolates
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Monteverde cloud forest lodge – warming highland cuisine featuring local cheeses (Monteverde is Costa Rica's cheese capital), hearty stews, artisan bread, local craft beer or wine

day_by_day.notes: The jeep-boat-jeep transfer from La Fortuna to Monteverde is a scenic adventure in itself and is highly recommended over the longer road route. Monteverde is cooler and misty – pack a light rain jacket and layers. February is peak quetzal season so request a specialized quetzal-spotting guide.

day_by_day.morning: The highlight of the Monteverde experience – the Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour. Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits featuring multiple cables, Tarzan swings, rappels, and a thrilling Superman cable. Enjoy breathtaking views of the cloud forest canopy, the Gulf of Nicoya, and on clear days, Arenal Volcano in the distance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve for a private guided hike through the Continental Divide trail – walk through five distinct ecological zones and experience the mystical cloud forest draped in mosses, bromeliads, and orchids. Spot resplendent quetzals in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local artisan cheese factory for a premium cheese and wine tasting – Monteverde's dairy heritage is world-renowned. Return to lodge for a final cloud forest dinner with live local music.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge before zip-lining – energy-rich meal with eggs, whole grains, fresh fruit, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Post-zip-line lunch at a Monteverde restaurant – Restaurante Celajes with panoramic cloud forest views; Costa Rican casado with fresh local trout or heart of palm dishes
meals.dinner: Farewell Monteverde dinner at the lodge – five-course tasting menu featuring local Monteverde cheeses, cloud forest mushrooms, locally raised beef, and artisan desserts; pair with Costa Rican craft spirits

day_by_day.notes: The zip-line tour has weight restrictions (typically 100kg/220lbs maximum). Wear closed-toe shoes and avoid loose clothing or jewelry. The cloud forest is frequently misty which actually enhances the zip-line experience with a magical atmosphere. Book the first morning slot for the best wildlife sightings along the zip-line platforms.

day_by_day.morning: Final cloud forest morning – early guided bird walk at dawn for last chance quetzal and bellbird sightings. Visit the Hummingbird Gallery adjacent to the cloud forest reserve where dozens of hummingbird species feed at close range. Purchase artisan souvenirs from local Monteverde craftspeople and cooperatives.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Monteverde back to the Pacific coast and Aegean Bliss Resort (approximately 3–4 hours). Arrive at the resort and enjoy a welcome-back swim in the ocean or pool. Arrange a premium spa treatment – deep tissue massage, volcanic clay body wrap, or couples' treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner at the resort's finest dining venue – request the chef's table experience or a private beachside dinner set up on the sand with torches, personalized menu, and sommelier-selected wine pairing. Stargaze on the beach after dinner.

meals.breakfast: Final cloud forest breakfast at Monteverde lodge – leisurely and indulgent; fresh fruit platter, eggs Benedict, artisan pastries, local cheeses, specialty Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: En-route lunch stop at a premium restaurant in Puntarenas or Jacó – fresh Pacific seafood; ceviche, grilled snapper, patacones with guacamole
meals.dinner: Private beachside chef's table dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort – personalized multi-course menu celebrating the best of Costa Rican cuisine; lobster, prime beef tenderloin, tropical desserts; premium wine and champagne pairing

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the private beachside dinner setup with the resort at least 48 hours in advance. This is the final full evening – make it memorable. Consider arranging a surprise celebration element (flowers, champagne, personalized dessert) if traveling with a partner. Pack purchased souvenirs carefully for the journey home.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the resort beach – collect shells, watch pelicans dive, and soak in the last moments of Costa Rican paradise. Enjoy a leisurely farewell breakfast at the resort. Complete packing and check out. Arrange for the resort to store luggage if departure flight is in the afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, enjoy final resort amenities – pool, beach, or a short guided mangrove kayak tour near the resort. Private luxury transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO) in San José – allow at least 3–3.5 hours before departure including transfer time.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with extraordinary memories of cloud forests, volcanoes, wildlife, and Caribbean and Pacific coastlines. Access the premium airport lounge at SJO for pre-flight comfort.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – your favorite items from the week; fresh tropical fruits, eggs, gallo pinto, artisan pastries, specialty Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or airport – keep it simple before the flight; fresh ceviche, tropical fruit, sparkling water
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge dining at SJO

day_by_day.notes: Costa Rica's SJO airport recommends arriving 3 hours before international flights. Confirm private transfer timing with the resort concierge the evening before. Declare any food items (coffee, chocolate, spices) at customs. Consider purchasing premium Costa Rican coffee, Britt chocolates, or artisan rum at the airport as final gifts. Pura Vida!

query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami
